runs.text: The room-temperature run was a comparison, not the intended process. The authors wanted to show what happens when the PVDF/Cyrene mixture is allowed to cool. Their proposed separation is done hot, because controlling temperature is critical:

runs.quote: PVDF would precipitate out if the temperature was low

runs.text: . In the FTIR comparison, the cathode powder filtered at room temperature still showed the PVDF band, which the authors read as a sign of the reprecipitation of PVDF along with the cathode particles after cooling down to room temperature.

runs.quote: at 871 cm^−1 for the reclaimed powder that was filtered at high temperature

runs.text: lacked that band, which shows the binder had been removed. So the room-temperature filtration was run to demonstrate the re-precipitation problem that the hot filtration is designed to avoid.

rendered: The room-temperature run was a comparison, not the intended process. The authors wanted to show what happens when the PVDF/Cyrene mixture is allowed to cool. Their proposed separation is done hot, because controlling temperature is critical: PVDF would precipitate out if the temperature was low[1]. In the FTIR comparison, the cathode powder filtered at room temperature still showed the PVDF band, which the authors read as a sign of the reprecipitation of PVDF along with the cathode particles after cooling down to room temperature. at 871 cm^−1 for the reclaimed powder that was filtered at high temperature[2] lacked that band, which shows the binder had been removed. So the room-temperature filtration was run to demonstrate the re-precipitation problem that the hot filtration is designed to avoid.
